items.title: Love’s Greatest Happiness
items.summary: The union between Christ and his bride is so close that any good done to her is a good done to himself.

items.title: Jesus’s Joy in Marriage
items.summary: Jesus did not want a dirty and unholy wife. Therefore, he was willing to die to cleanse her so that he could present her to himself.

items.title: The Purpose of Prosperity
items.summary: You can steal to get; or you can work to get; or you can work to get in order to give.

items.title: Fear and Hope in God’s Jealousy
items.summary: It is a horrifying thing to use your God-given life to commit adultery against the Almighty.

items.title: Plan for Prayer
items.summary: One of the main reasons we so often fail to have consistent habits of happy, fruitful prayer is simply that we don’t plan to.

items.title: God Heals by Humbling
items.summary: God takes out our old proud hearts and gives new soft ones, which are easily humbled and crushed by the sin that remains.

items.title: The Master Servant
items.summary: The very heart of God’s glory is the fullness of grace that overflows in kindness to needy people.

items.title: Can My Pain Kill My Sins?
items.summary: Does suffering kill the sin within us? Pastor John argues from 1 Peter 4:1 that believers die to sin with Christ so we can live to his righteousness.

items.title: Trapped in a Meaningless Life
items.summary: Loss can lead to despair over God’s plan for our lives. When we can’t perceive meaning in life, Pastor John counsels us to find comfort in God’s glorious purpose in Christ.

items.title: Do Good People Get Hurt?
items.summary: Does the Bible promise that believers will not be harmed for doing good? Pastor John explains the context of 1 Peter 3:13 and God’s sovereign wisdom in suffering.

items.title: The Marriage Miracle That Takes Time
items.summary: Loving our spouses for better or worse includes loving them through their spiritual apathy. Pastor John gives ten encouragements for the weary.

items.title: When You’re Not Sorry
items.summary: When someone confronts you wrongly, should you apologize? Pastor John encourages humility and reconciliation without giving in to emotional manipulation.

items.title: The Gospel Before Jesus Died
items.summary: Did Jesus preach the gospel before his death and resurrection? Pastor John calls us to a deeper understanding of God as Creator and King, and Jesus as Lord and Savior.

items.title: Enduring Grace
items.summary: In the last 40 years or so, we’ve had an explosion of 12-step groups helping people with a range of addictions. And even if you don’t have those addictions, think of how much misery there is in our lives because we can’t control our tongue or our time or our thoughts. Just about everybody has a problem with…

items.title: Passionate Grace
items.summary: A lot of people think that to say Christians have a changed relationship to the truth means that Christians become honest. It’s not less than that. Technical, ethical honesty is one thing. But we’re talking about something more and deeper. In Ephesians 4:15, Paul says, “speaking the truth in love.” But what Paul…

items.title: Blessed Self-Forgetfulness
items.summary: To talk about humility means we’re getting into a very culturally interesting subject, which is self-esteem. Traditional cultures have believed that having too high a view of yourself is the real root cause for most of the evil in the world. But in modern Western culture, particularly in the United States, we have an…

items.title: Receptive Grace
items.summary: How can you relate to someone whose views and values and practices offend you and distress you? How can we relate to people with whom we deeply differ? Our culture says we need to be tolerant, but I want to show you that Paul says the mark of a supernaturally changed heart is to go way beyond tolerance. It’s…

items.title: Resting Grace
items.summary: One trait or quality of a supernaturally changed heart is peace. There’s a difference between a supernaturally changed heart and a morally restrained heart. The marks of a supernaturally changed heart are sometimes called the fruit of the Spirit. They’re listed a number of places in the New Testament. And peace is…

items.title: Befriending Grace
items.summary: Every religion in the world gives you a list of virtuous behaviors. But the New Testament gives you something different. It does give you a list, but it’s of aspects of how a supernaturally, grace-changed heart shows itself. The apostle Paul says it’s possible to do all the morally virtuous behavior without any love…

items.title: The Reward of the Believer
items.summary: Our prize isn't something we earn through performance—it's the joy of living a life rooted in Christ.

items.title: The Work of the Believer
items.summary: God gave each of us unique gifts for a shared purpose: to serve others and glorify Him.

items.title: Strength for the Task
items.summary: The God who helped David defeat Goliath is the same God standing with you today.

items.title: The Victorious Life
items.summary: We all face giants, but we never have to face them alone—the Lord fights beside us.

items.title: The Faithfulness of God
items.summary: Living a truly honorable life is only possible when we build our foundation on the Lord.

items.title: What We Could Never Earn
items.summary: Salvation isn't earned—it's freely given through Christ, who conquered sin to set us free.

items.title: The Gift of Salvation
items.summary: Experience true, complete freedom by accepting the gift of salvation.

items.title: Blessed for God's Own Glory (2 Chronicles 9:8)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 9:8, David Platt reminds us that God blesses his people for his own glory among the nations. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Trust Christ’s Sacrifice (2 Chronicles 8:12–13)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 8:12–13, David Platt reminds Christians of the blessing of the sacrifice of Christ. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Every Nation and Tribe (2 Chronicles 6:32–33)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 6:32–33, David Platt reminds us that one day every nation, tribe, and tongue will worship God. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Faithful Stewards of the Body (2 Chronicles 5:13–14)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 5:13–14, David Platt calls us to steward our bodies for the glory of God. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Perfect Communion with God (2 Chronicles 3:8)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 3:8, David Platt explains the Christian hope of perfect, eternal communion with God. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: The Biblical Call for Wisdom (2 Chronicles 1:10–12)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 1:10–12, David Platt emphasizes the importance of prioritizing wisdom over worldly desires. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Joy in Giving (1 Chronicles 29:9)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 29:9, David Platt explains the joy of giving for the glory of Christ. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: God’s Love Begins With Him, Not You
items.summary: God’s love is not something we earn through our obedience, nor is it an excuse to continue in sin. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how God’s love flows from His character, is revealed through Jesus Christ, and transforms how we love others. Resources: In Jesus' Name I Pray: TJ the Squirrel Learns the True Heart…

items.title: When God’s Glory Exposes Your Sin
items.summary: We are often quick to recognize the sins of others while overlooking our own. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how seeing God in His holiness strips away our excuses, exposes our sin, and calls us to genuine repentance.

items.title: You Can Know God But Never Master Him
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be incomprehensible. God is infinitely greater than our minds can comprehend, yet He has made Himself truly knowable through His Word and ultimately through Jesus Christ.

items.title: Your View of God Shapes Everything
items.summary: You may not deny God, but do you diminish Him? In this episode, Costi Hinn examines how a small or distorted view of God can shape the way we live, exposing the gap between what we confess about God and how we actually function day to day.

items.title: No One Is Above God
items.summary: The name El Elyon means “God Most High,” declaring God’s absolute supremacy over everyone and everything. In this final episode of the Names of God series, Costi Hinn explains what it means to live with the perspective that God is sovereign, owns everything, and answers to no one.
